NXS TCS Article — Reports

IPBES TCA & Nexus assessment corpus: embeddings, keypaper similarity, topics

Author

Rainer M. Krug

Published

August 5, 2026

This is the landing page for the NXS TCS Article analysis. The corpus is built from two curated IPBES assessment Zotero groups — TCA and NXS — matched to OpenAlex works and extracted from a local snapshot. Each work is embedded with SPECTER2 (title, abstract, and title+abstract variants) and scored by cosine similarity against a curated set of TCA/Nexus keypaper concept definitions. Inline citations in the definitions are extracted and resolved to a cited corpus, and the key-sets are linked to one another (notably TCA Action ↔︎ Nexus Response Option) via three similarity stages.

The analysis is split across three reports, described below. Each opens in the output/reports/ folder alongside this page; a link resolves once that report has been rendered (targets::tar_make()).

Embedding Report

Embedding quality control: corpus coverage (title / abstract presence and counts), language mix, input text length and silent truncation at the 512-token limit, work-type counts, title vs abstract variant agreement, and embedding-norm sanity checks. Read this to judge whether the embeddings are trustworthy before interpreting the analysis.

Chapter Analysis Report

The main analysis: how close the papers in each assessment / chapter are to the keypaper concepts, plus keyset linkage — how the concept definitions link to one another (notably TCA Action ↔︎ Nexus Response Option) across three stages (definition-embedding similarity, cited-literature overlap, and cited-literature embedding similarity) with Sankey diagrams. Also overall chapter alignment (median similarity with bootstrap 95% CIs), Cliff’s δ, the chapter × keypaper heatmap, an interactive per-keypaper top-matches browser, corpus-wide keypaper-relevance, and keypaper-set diagnostics.

Topic modelling (BERTopic) is disabled in this configuration.

Citation Method Comparison Report

Compares the two citation-identification methods — the deterministic regex parser and the LLM (OpenRouter) parser — that extract the in-text citations from the definitions: extraction volume, agreement per keyset, and resolution rate (a precision proxy) to judge which performs better.

The targets pipeline that produces these reports — from the two IPBES Zotero groups through embeddings, keypaper scoring, citation resolution and keyset linkage. (Source: input/mmd/pipeline.mmd.)
